Main.sentence: The Arab League ( ___E:Arabic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language)___ : الجامعة العربية , al-Jāmiʿa al-ʻArabiyya [al.d͡ʒaː.mi.ʕa al.ʕa.ra.bij.ja] ⓘ ), officially the League of Arab States ( ___E:Arabic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language)___ : جامعة الدول العربية , Jāmiʿat ad-Duwal al-ʿArabiyya ), is a ___E:regional organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regional_organization)___ in the ___E:Arab world U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_world)___ .

The Arab League was formed in ___E:Cairo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cairo)___ on 22 March 1945, initially with seven members: ___E:Egypt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Egypt)___ , ___E:Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Iraq)___ , ___E:Transjordan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emirate_of_Transjordan)___ , ___E:Lebanon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon)___ , ___E:Saudi Arabia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabia)___ , ___E:Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Syrian_Republic)___ , and ___E:North Yemen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Yemen)___ .
Currently, the League has ___E:22 members U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_states_of_the_Arab_League)___ .

The League's main goal is to "draw closer the relations between member states and co-ordinate collaboration between them, to safeguard their independence and sovereignty, and to consider in a general way the affairs and interests of the Arab countries".
The organization has received a relatively low level of cooperation throughout its history.

Through institutions, notably the ___E:Arab League Educational, Cultural and Scientific Organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_League_Educational,_Cultural_and_Scientific_Organization)___ (ALECSO) and the Economic and Social Council of its ___E:Council of Arab Economic Unity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_Arab_Economic_Unity)___ (CAEU), the League facilitates political, economic, cultural, scientific, and social programmes designed to promote the interests of the Arab world.

It has served as a forum for the member states to coordinate policy, arrange studies of and committees as to matters of common concern, settle inter-state disputes and limit conflicts such as the ___E:1958 Lebanon crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1958_Lebanon_crisis)___ .
The League has served as a platform for the drafting and conclusion of many landmark documents promoting economic integration.

One example is the ___E:Joint Arab Economic Action Charter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Arab_Economic_Action_Charter)___ , which outlines the principles for economic activities in the region.

Each member state has one vote in the ___E:Council of the Arab League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_the_Arab_League)___ , and decisions are binding only for those states that have voted for them. The aims of the league in 1945 were to strengthen and coordinate the political, cultural, economic and social programs of its members and to mediate disputes among them or between them and third parties.
Furthermore, the signing of an agreement on Joint Defence and Economic Cooperation on 13 April 1950 committed the signatories to coordination of military defence measures.
In March 2015, the Arab League General Secretary announced the establishment of a Joint Arab Force with the aim of counteracting extremism and other threats to the Arab States.
The decision was reached while ___E:Operation Decisive Storm U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Decisive_Storm)___ was intensifying in Yemen.
Participation in the project is voluntary, and the army intervenes only at the request of one of the member states.
Existing military cooperation between Arab league states and regional civil wars and terrorist threats were the impetuses for JAF's establishment.

In the early 1970s, the Economic Council put forward a proposal to create the ___E:Joint Arab Chambers of Commerce U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politics_of_the_Arab_League)___ across international states.
That led to the setting up of mandates to promote, encourage and facilitate bilateral trade between the Arab world and significant trading partners.

Following adoption of the ___E:Alexandria Protocol U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexandria_Protocol)___ in 1944, the Arab League was founded on 22 March 1945.  The official headquarters of the League was the Boustan Palace in Cairo.
It aimed to be a regional organisation of Arab states with a focus to developing the economy, resolving disputes and coordinating political aims.  Other countries later joined the league.
Each country was given one vote in the council.
The first major action was joint intervention to keep Palestine from being divided into two states in keeping with the decision of the United Nations General Assembly.
When Transjordan agreed to this proposal, Egypt intervened to prevent this from happening.
It was followed by the creation of a mutual defence treaty two years later.
A common market was established in 1965.
The Arab League has not achieved much cooperation throughout its history.

According to ___E:Michael Barnett U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_N._Barnett)___ and ___E:Etel Solingen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etel_Solingen)___ , the design of the Arab League reflects Arab leaders' individual concerns for regime survival: "the politics of Arab nationalism and a shared identity led Arab states to embrace the rhetoric of Arab unity in order to legitimize their regimes, and to fear Arab unity in practice because it would impose greater restrictions on their sovereignty."  The Arab League was "specifically designed to fail at producing the kind of greater collaboration and integration that might have weakened political leaders at home."

The Arab League member states cover over 13,000,000 km 2 (5,000,000 sq mi) and straddles two continents: ___E:Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa)___ and ___E:Asia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asia)___ .
The area largely consists of arid deserts, such as the ___E:Sahara U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahara)___ .

Nevertheless, it also contains several highly fertile lands like the ___E:Nile Valley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nile_Valley)___ , the ___E:Jubba Valley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jubba_Valley)___ and ___E:Shebelle Valley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shebelle_Valley)___ in the ___E:Horn of Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horn_of_Africa)___ , the ___E:Atlas Mountains U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlas_Mountains)___ in the ___E:Maghreb U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maghreb)___ , and the ___E:Fertile Crescent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fertile_Crescent)___ that stretches over ___E:Mesopotamia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesopotamia)___ and the ___E:Levant U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Levant)___ .

The area comprises deep forests in southern ___E:Arabia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Peninsula)___ and parts of the world's longest river, the ___E:Nile U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nile)___ .
The ___E:Charter of the Arab League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charter_of_the_Arab_League)___ , also known as the Pact of the League of Arab States, is the founding treaty of the Arab League.
Adopted in 1945, it stipulates that "the League of Arab States shall be composed of the independent Arab States that have signed this Pact."
In 1945, there were seven members,  but the Arab League now has 22 members, including 10 African countries:
and 7 observer states (note: the observer states below have been invited to participate during select Arab League sessions but do not hold voting privileges):

___E:Egypt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt)___ was suspended from the Arab League on 26 March 1979 due to the ___E:Egypt–Israel peace treaty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt%E2%80%93Israel_peace_treaty)___ , with the League's headquarters moving from Cairo to ___E:Tunis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunis)___ , Tunisia.
In 1987, Arab League states restored diplomatic relations with Egypt, the country was readmitted to the League in May 1989 and the League's headquarters were moved back to Cairo in September 1990.

___E:Libya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libya)___ was suspended on 22 February 2011, following the outbreak of the ___E:first Libyan civil war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Libyan_civil_war)___ .

The Arab League voted to restore Libya's membership on 27 August 2011 by accrediting a representative of the ___E:National Transitional Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Transitional_Council)___ , which was the partially recognised interim government of the country.

___E:Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria)___ was suspended on 16 November 2011 in the aftermath of the outbreak of the ___E:Syrian civil war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_civil_war)___ .

On 6 March 2013, the Arab League gave Syria's seat in the Arab League to the ___E:Syrian National Coalition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_National_Coalition)___ , the largest ___E:opposition group U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_opposition_to_Bashar_al-Assad)___ .

On 9 March 2014, secretary general ___E:Nabil Elaraby U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nabil_Elaraby)___ stated that Syria's seat would remain vacant until the opposition completed the formation of its institutions.
In 2021, the Arab League initiated a process of normalisation between the ___E:Syrian Ba'athist government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ba%27athist_Syria)___ and other Arab nations.
On 7 May 2023, at the meeting of the ___E:Council of the Arab League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Council_of_the_Arab_League)___ in Cairo, it was agreed to reinstate Syria's membership.
The Arab League is a political organization which tries to help integrate its members economically, and solve conflicts involving member states without asking for foreign assistance.
It possesses elements of a state representative parliament while foreign affairs are often conducted under UN supervision.

The Charter of the Arab League  endorsed the principle of an ___E:Arab nation-state U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pan-Arabism)___ while respecting the ___E:sovereignty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sovereignty)___ of the individual member states.
The internal regulations of the Council of the League  and the committees  were agreed in October 1951. Those of the Secretariat-General were agreed in May 1953.
Since then, governance of the Arab League has been based on the duality of supra-national institutions and the sovereignty of the member states.
Preservation of individual statehood derived its strengths from the natural preference of ruling elites to maintain their power and independence in decision making.

Moreover, the fear of the richer that the poorer may share their wealth in the name of ___E:Arab nationalism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_nationalism)___ , the ___E:feuds among Arab rulers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_Cold_War)___ , and the influence of external powers that might oppose Arab unity can be seen as obstacles towards a deeper integration of the league.

Mindful of their previous announcements in support of the ___E:Arabs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabs)___ of ___E:Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine)___ the framers of the Pact were determined to include them within the League from its inauguration.
This was done by means of an annex that declared:

Even though Palestine was not able to control her own destiny, it was on the basis of the recognition of her independence that the Covenant of the League of Nations determined a system of government for her. Her existence and her independence among the nations can, therefore, no more be questioned de jure than the independence of any of the other Arab States. [...] Therefore, the States signatory to the Pact of the Arab League consider that in view of Palestine's special circumstances, the Council of the League should designate an Arab delegate from Palestine to participate in its work until this country enjoys actual independence

In September 1963, the Arab League appointed ___E:Ahmad Shukeiri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmad_Shukeiri)___ as Representative of Palestine at the Arab League.  : xxviii At the Cairo Summit of 1964, the Arab League initiated the creation of an organisation representing the Palestinian people.

The first ___E:Palestinian National Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_National_Council)___ convened in ___E:East Jerusalem U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Jerusalem)___ on 29 May 1964. The ___E:Palestine Liberation Organization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine_Liberation_Organization)___ was founded during this meeting on 2 June 1964. Palestine was shortly admitted in to the Arab League, represented by the PLO. Today, ___E:State of Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_Palestine)___ is a full member of the Arab League.

At the ___E:Beirut Summit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beirut_Summit)___ on 28 March 2002, the league adopted the ___E:Arab Peace Initiative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_Peace_Initiative)___ ,  a Saudi-inspired peace plan for the ___E:Arab–Israeli conflict U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab%E2%80%93Israeli_conflict)___ .
The initiative offered full normalisation of the relations with ___E:Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel)___ .

In exchange, Israel was required to withdraw from all ___E:occupied territories U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli-occupied_territories)___ , including the ___E:Golan Heights U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golan_Heights)___ , to recognise Palestinian independence in the ___E:West Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank)___ and ___E:Gaza Strip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip)___ , with East Jerusalem as its capital, as well as a "just solution" for the ___E:Palestinian refugees U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinian_refugees)___ .
The Peace Initiative was again endorsed at 2007 in the Riyadh Summit.

In July 2007, the Arab League sent a mission, consisting of the ___E:Jordanian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan)___ and ___E:Egyptian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt)___ foreign ministers, to Israel to promote the initiative.

Following ___E:Venezuela U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuela)___ 's move to expel Israeli diplomats amid the ___E:2008–2009 Israel–Gaza conflict U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%932009_Israel%E2%80%93Gaza_conflict)___ , ___E:Kuwaiti U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuwait)___ member of parliament ___E:Waleed Al-Tabtabaie U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waleed_Al-Tabtabaie)___ proposed moving Arab League headquarters to ___E:Caracas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caracas,_Venezuela)___ , ___E:Venezuela U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuela)___ .

On 13 June 2010, Amr Mohammed Moussa, Secretary-General of the Arab League, visited the ___E:Gaza Strip U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_Strip)___ , the first visit by an official of the Arab League since Hamas' armed takeover in 2007.

The Arab League is a member of the ___E:China-Arab States Cooperation Forum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China-Arab_States_Cooperation_Forum)___ (CASCF), which was formed in 2004. CASCF is the Arab League's earliest participation in a cooperation forum with another country or region.
CASCF is the primarily multi-lateral coordination mechanism between the Arab states and China and within CASCF the Arab League represents its member states as a relatively unified force.
The Arab League's coordination allows Arab states to negotiate actively for collective projects involving multiple states, such as railway projects, nuclear power projects, and Dead Sea initiatives.

In 2015, the Arab League voiced support for ___E:Saudi Arabian-led military intervention in Yemen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabian-led_intervention_in_Yemen)___ against the ___E:Shia Houthis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaidiyyah)___ and forces loyal to former President ___E:Ali Abdullah Saleh U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Abdullah_Saleh)___ , who was deposed in the ___E:2011 uprising U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yemeni_Revolution)___ .

On 15 April 2018, in response to the ___E:Turkish invasion of northern Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Olive_Branch)___ aimed at ousting U.S.-backed ___E:Syrian Kurds U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People%27s_Protection_Units)___ from the enclave of ___E:Afrin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrin,_Syria)___ , the Arab League passed a resolution calling on Turkish forces to withdraw from Afrin.

In September 2019, the Arab League condemned ___E:Benjamin Netanyahu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Netanyahu)___ 's plans to ___E:annex U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annexation)___ the eastern portion of the occupied ___E:West Bank U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bank)___ known as the ___E:Jordan Valley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Valley)___ .
The Arab League met in Cairo on 12 October 2019 to discuss ___E:Turkish offensive into north-eastern Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Turkish_offensive_into_north-eastern_Syria)___ .

Upon meeting, its member states voted to condemn the Turkish offensive, dubbing it both an 'invasion' and an 'aggression' against an Arab state, adding that the organization saw it as a violation of international law.

On 9 September 2020, the Arab League refused to condemn the ___E:UAE U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates)___ 's decision to ___E:normalize ties with Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel%E2%80%93United_Arab_Emirates_peace_agreement)___ .

Nevertheless, "The goal all our Arab countries seek, without exception, is to end the occupation and establish an independent Palestinian state on the 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital," ___E:Aboul Gheit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Aboul_Gheit)___ said.  In January 2024, the Arab League expressed support for South Africa's ___E:ICJ genocide case U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa_v._Israel_(Genocide_Convention))___ against Israel.
The Joint Defence Council of the Arab League is one of the ___E:Institutions of the Arab League U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institutions_of_the_Arab_League)___ .

It was established under the terms of the ___E:Joint Defence and Economic Co-operation Treaty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_Defence_and_Economic_Co-operation_Treaty)___ of 1950 to coordinate the ___E:joint defence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collective_security)___ of the Arab League ___E:member states U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Member_states_of_the_Arab_League)___ .

The Arab League as an organisation has no military Force, similar to the UN, but at the 2007 summit, the Leaders decided to reactivate their joint defence and establish a peacekeeping force to deploy in South Lebanon, Darfur, Iraq, and other hot spots.
At a 2015 summit in Egypt, member states agreed in principle to form a joint military force.

The Arab League is rich in resources, such as enormous ___E:oil U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil)___ and ___E:natural gas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_gas)___ resources in certain member states.

Economic achievements initiated by the League amongst member states have been less impressive than those achieved by smaller Arab organisations such as the ___E:Gulf Cooperation Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Cooperation_Council)___ (GCC).
Among them is the ___E:Arab Gas Pipeline U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_Gas_Pipeline)___ , that will transport Egyptian and Iraqi gas to Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, and Turkey.

As of 2013, a significant difference in economic conditions exist between the developed oil states of ___E:Algeria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algeria)___ , ___E:Qatar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qatar)___ , ___E:Kuwait U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuwait)___ and the ___E:UAE U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UAE)___ , and developing countries like the ___E:Comoros U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comoros)___ , ___E:Djibouti U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Djibouti)___ , ___E:Mauritania U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauritania)___ , ___E:Somalia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somalia)___ , ___E:Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan)___ and ___E:Yemen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yemen)___ .
The Arab League also includes great fertile lands in the southern part of ___E:Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan)___ .

It is referred to as the food basket of the ___E:Arab World U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_World)___ , the region's instability including the independence of ___E:South Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Sudan)___ has not affected its ___E:tourism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism)___ industry, that is considered the fastest growing industry in the region, with ___E:Egypt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt)___ , ___E:UAE U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UAE)___ , ___E:Lebanon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon)___ , ___E:Tunisia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunisia)___ , and ___E:Jordan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan)___ leading the way. Another industry that is growing steadily in the Arab League is telecommunications.

Economical achievements within members have been low in the league's history, other smaller Arab Organizations have achieved more than the league has, such as the ___E:GCC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooperation_Council_for_the_Arab_States_of_the_Gulf)___ , but lately several major economic projects that are promising are to be completed, the ___E:Arab Gas Pipeline U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arab_Gas_Pipeline)___ is to end by 2010, Connecting Egyptian and Iraqi Gas to Jordan, Syria and Lebanon, and then to Turkey thus Europe, a free trade Agreement ( ___E:GAFTA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_Arab_Free_Trade_Area)___ ) is to be completed by 1 January 2008, making 95% of all Arab products tax free of customs.

The Arab League is divided into five parts when it comes to transport, with the ___E:Arabian Peninsula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Peninsula)___ and the ___E:Near East U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Near_East)___ being entirely connected by air, sea, roads and railways.

Another part of the League is the ___E:Nile Valley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nile_Valley)___ , made up of ___E:Egypt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt)___ and ___E:Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan)___ .
These two member states have started to improve the River Nile's navigation system to improve accessibility and thus foster trading.

A new railway system is also set to connect the southern Egyptian city of ___E:Abu Simbel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abu_Simbel)___ with the northern Sudanese city of ___E:Wadi Halfa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wadi_Halfa)___ and then to ___E:Khartoum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khartoum)___ and ___E:Port Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_Sudan)___ .

The third division of the League is the ___E:Maghreb U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maghreb)___ , where a 3,000 km stretch of railway runs from the southern cities of ___E:Morocco U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco)___ to ___E:Tripoli U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tripoli,_Libya)___ in Western ___E:Libya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libya)___ .

The fourth division of the League is the ___E:Horn of Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horn_of_Africa)___ , whose member states include ___E:Djibouti U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Djibouti)___ and ___E:Somalia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somalia)___ .

These two Arab League states are separated by only ten nautical miles from the Arabian Peninsula by the ___E:Bab el Mandeb U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bab_el_Mandeb)___ and this is quickly changing as Tarik bin Laden, the brother of ___E:Osama bin Laden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osama_bin_Laden)___ , has initiated the construction of the ambitious ___E:Bridge of the Horns U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridge_of_the_Horns)___ project, which ultimately aims to connect the ___E:Horn of Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horn_of_Africa)___ with the ___E:Arabian Peninsula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Peninsula)___ via a massive bridge.
The project is intended to facilitate and accelerate the already centuries-old trade and commerce between the two regions.

The last division of the League is the isolated archipelago of the ___E:Comoros U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comoros)___ located off the coast of ___E:East Africa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Africa)___ , which is not physically connected to any other Arab state, but still trades with other Arab League members.

In collecting literacy data, many countries estimate the number of literate people based on self-reported data. Some use educational attainment data as a proxy, but measures of school attendance or grade completion may differ.

Because definitions and data collection methods vary across countries, literacy estimates should be used with caution. ___E:United Nations Development Programme U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Development_Programme)___ , ___E:Human Development Report U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Development_Report)___ 2010. The ___E:Persian Gulf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Persian_Gulf)___ region has had an ___E:oil boom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oil_boom)___ , enabling more schools and universities to be set up.

While ___E:Egyptians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egyptians)___ constitute the largest ethnic group in the Arab League, there are several other ethnic groups that also reside in the region, including ___E:Arabs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabs)___ , ___E:Berbers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berbers)___ , ___E:Kurds U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurds)___ , ___E:Somalis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somalis)___ , ___E:Assyrians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assyrian_people)___ , ___E:Armenians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armenians)___ , ___E:Nubians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nubians)___ , ___E:Mandaeans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandaeans)___ , and ___E:Circassians U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circassians)___ .
Each of these groups have their own distinct cultures, languages, and traditions.
As of 1 July 2013, about 359 million people live in the states of the Arab League.
Its population grows faster than in most other global regions.
The most populous member state is ___E:Egypt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt)___ , with a population of over 100 million.
The least populated is the ___E:Comoros U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comoros)___ , with approximately 850,000 inhabitants.

The majority of the Arab League's citizens adhere to ___E:Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islam)___ , with ___E:Christianity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity)___ being the second largest religion.

At least 15 million Christians combined live in ___E:Egypt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt)___ , ___E:Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq)___ , ___E:Jordan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan)___ , ___E:Lebanon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lebanon)___ , ___E:Palestine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestine)___ , ___E:Sudan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan)___ and ___E:Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syria)___ .

In addition, there are smaller but significant numbers of ___E:Druze U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Druze)___ , ___E:Yazidis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yazidis)___ , ___E:Shabaks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabak_people)___ and ___E:Mandaeans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandaeans)___ .

Numbers for nonreligious ___E:Arabs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabs)___ are generally not available, but research by the ___E:Pew Forum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pew_Forum)___ suggests around 1% of people in the ___E:MENA U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MENA)___ region are "unaffiliated".

The official language of the Arab League is ___E:Literary Arabic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Standard_Arabic)___ , based on ___E:Classical Arabic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classical_Arabic)___ .
